session_results.attack: Three separate overscopes, and one of them is a layer error. (1) "Robinson was not identified by investigators" is flatter than the testimony it rests on. Hull's actual answer to that exact question was qualified: asked whether "as of the moment that Tyler Robinson voluntarily surrendered... you all did not know who the shooter was," he said "We had identified a PERSON OF INTEREST, but we did not specifically know who the shooter was at that time" (day2 01:52:15). Investigators had the shooter's image, route, gait, rooftop position and vehicle; what they lacked was a name. (2) "until he surrendered" is off by the interval that matters: the name reached SBI BEFORE the surrender, not at it. Hull: "on the evening of the 11th, we received word from Washington County that an individual... was wanting to turn themselves in" and "did you receive a name from Washington County? Yes we did... Tyler Robinson" (day1 06:31:59-06:32:25), after which SIAC pulled his DL photo, address, DOB and vehicle. Davis dates that call to ~8:30 PM and Robinson's arrival at the sheriff's office to ~9:00 PM (day3 34:06, 36:51); the court's findings add a Discord post "just before 8:00 PM" announcing the surrender (2026-09-01, 07:54-07:56). So the identity was known ~30-60 minutes before the walk-in. (3) The hardest hit: "The case begins with a family recognising a photograph" is NOT sworn testimony. I searched all five hearing days and the final-argument day for mother/father/recognise/news — nothing. The hearing record's account is Hull's: "He had informed, I believe, his immediate family that he had been involved in the shooting and that he wanted to turn himself in" (day2 02:23:13), plus the court's findings, which contain no photo-recognition finding at all. The mother-sees-the-news-photo story lives in the sworn probable-cause statement of the 2025-09-16 Information — a charging affidavit, not testimony. Attributing it to "sworn testimony" moves a claimant-layer summary into the analyst layer. A further attack I could not land: the prosecutor's final argument says Officer Goforth ran the partial plate from a 12:36 AM 9/11 stop, got the registration to "the defendant and his mother" and matched his DL photo (03:50:47-03:51:20) — which would be a pre-surrender name-identification by an investigator. Hull's underlying testimony defeats it on timing: Goforth ran the plate "subsequently, when information was available that that vehicle... was involved in the incident" (day2 00:58:38), which is undated and may post-date the surrender. Recorded as not established rather than as a refutation. Finally, "not with detection" forecloses the obvious alternative: the photograph the family reacted to was itself a product of the surveillance review investigators ran and released.

session_results.attack:
Three separate overreaches, one of which the record refutes outright.

(1) "or when" is NOT unqualified — the record qualifies it twice, once by the State's own cross. Bakker (FBI) on direct: "I can't give an exact time, but there are some situations... it would be my expectation... that I probably won't get DNA off of an item that's been buried for 10 years" (day2.txt, Bakker 05:31:44). Then on the State's cross McBride narrowed the proposition to "the EXACT time" and Bakker agreed there are indicators beyond it: "But there are some indicators that may give some information about how long and the conditions under which DNA was placed on an item, like degradation? — Yes, degradation or the condition of the item... something that's been left behind 10 years ago, I don't necessarily expect to recover DNA, but something that may have been left yesterday, I might be able to detect DNA" (day2.txt, 08:01:46–08:02:41). Oliver (ATF) likewise: "DNA is quite stable over time. It can be broken down due to environmental insults... but I couldn't give you an exact number" (day5.txt, 01:45:21). The agreed proposition is that they cannot give an EXACT time and cannot opine on activity — not that DNA carries no temporal information at all. "Unqualified" is false as written.

(2) A policy limit written as a capability limit. Bakker's activity-level answer is framed as an FBI reporting policy on OPINING: "does your laboratory have a policy about whether you can express opinions about formal activity level? — We do have a policy, and I cannot give an opinion as far as activity level goes" (day2.txt, 05:30:55–05:31:04). Oliver's is capability-framed ("None of the testing that I performed could speak to activity", day5.txt 01:34:09). "Neither can say" flattens a declining-to-opine rule into an epistemic impossibility.

(3) The superlative is an unfalsifiable count with no denominator. "The single most consistent proposition in the entire body of evidence" names no set, no comparator and no metric, and no source in the record decides it. It is also beatable on its face: propositions attested by far more witnesses across all five days (that Kirk was shot at ~12:23 on 2025-09-10; that a bolt-action .30-06 wrapped in a towel was recovered in the wooded area) are at least as consistent. This sentence is analyst-layer editorialising that its citations cannot carry.

What survived attack: "both laboratories" is correct — DNA in this record went to exactly two labs (Faumuina, day2.txt 05:04:38–05:04:48: "the gun went to the ATF lab... The towel went to the FBI lab... the screwdriver went to the FBI lab"; the Utah Bureau of Forensic Services did scene processing and latent prints, not DNA). And "unrebutted" survives narrowly: the State presented no rebuttal evidence (day5.txt, McBride 02:23:31: "We have no rebuttal evidence to present at this hearing") and did not cross Oliver at all (day5.txt, 02:23:08). But a reader will misread "unrebutted" as "accepted": the court's bindover ruling neither adopts nor addresses the limitation, instead stating that "the FBI DNA analysis PLACES defendant's DNA on a screwdriver recovered at the crime scene" (2026-09-01_final-prelim-argument.txt, 08:09:14) — the source-attribution formulation both analysts said is not scientifically defensible — and mis-assigns the lab: "The FBI performed DNA testing on the screwdriver, towel, rifle, spent casings, and three unfired cartridges" (same file, 07:56:56), when the rifle and cartridges were tested by Oliver at ATF.

session_results.replacement: The forensic record naming him is large in volume and narrow in what it can bear. The two laboratories that did the DNA work — the FBI Laboratory (Amanda Bakker, Day 2) and the ATF Forensic Science Laboratory (Caitlin Oliver, Day 5) — each testified that their testing cannot identify the activity that deposited DNA on an item, and that they cannot state the time at which it was deposited. No witness contradicted either point: the State did not cross-examine Ms. Oliver and offered no rebuttal evidence (Day 5, 02:23:08, 02:23:31), and on cross it drew the same activity-level limitation from Ms. Bakker (Day 2, 08:01:34–08:01:45). Two qualifications belong on the record: the timing limitation was put and agreed as inability to give an *exact* time, with Ms. Bakker agreeing that degradation and the condition of an item give "some information about how long and the conditions under which DNA was placed on an item" (Day 2, 08:01:54–08:02:41); and the FBI limitation is stated as laboratory policy against opining on activity level as well as a scientific caution (Day 2, 05:31:04). The court's oral bindover ruling does not address either limitation. (§8.4)

session_results.attack:
False as written, and refuted twice over by sworn testimony. The claim is an unrestricted null - "No witness stated who operated the rifle's bolt" - and two witnesses stated exactly that.

First, Sgt. Faumuina on the render-safe at the scene: "because it is a bolt action gun, we would have to manipulate the bolt or the lever back" (day4.txt 04:50:27); "Were you present when this weapon was made safe?" - "Yes, I was"; "when we rendered the gun safe, we found in it when we removed the bolt back, we found one 30 odd 6 cartridge case... and three unfired cartridges" (04:51:49-04:51:57). A named officer testified that her team, with her present, worked the bolt.

Second, and more decisive, ATF firearms examiner Samantha Karner: "I was asked to test fire the firearm and compare the test fires to the cartridge case and the bullet jacket fragment" (day4.txt 06:25:53); "How many test fires did you produce in this case?" - "I made three sets, so six total" (06:53:36). Six test fires from a rifle that the same record repeatedly establishes is bolt-action and that "requires a user to manipulate the bolt to load it, lock it, and extract anything that is in it" (court's ruling, final-argument 07:48:35). Karner necessarily and by her own testimony operated that bolt six times.

What is actually absent from the record is any witness identifying who worked the bolt to load and fire the round that killed Charlie Kirk - and the claim as written converts "no witness on the shooting" into "no witness at all," which is one witness's silence written as the record's. This matters more than a wording quibble: the second sentence tells the reader the null must never be read against a named person, and a null stated at the wrong scope is precisely how that safeguard fails.

session_results.attack: This was the one I most expected to break, and it holds on all four limbs. Wrong-laboratory attack FAILS: the examiner is 'a forensic examiner in the DNA Casework Unit of the FBI laboratory located in Quantico, Virginia,' and Sgt. Faumuina confirmed on the stand that the towel went to the FBI lab — so 'FBI item 7' is correct, not the Utah Bureau of Forensic Services. Wrong-exhibit attack FAILS: item 7 is identified on the record as 'Towel from around Mauser or rifle, Serial Number 8863,' and defence counsel pinned the three-contributor history to it by name — 'you originally determined in seven, SAMPLE SEVEN, that there were three contributors' / 'That is correct, yes.' Direction-of-travel attack FAILS: the movement is three→two, not two→three, and the examiner dated both calls (three ~Sept 12, 2025; changed Sept 13, 2025). 'Examiner's own call, input into the software' FAILS to break: asked 'who decides what the number of contributors is?' she answered 'That's my determination based on my experience and training,' and separately 'you input the number of contributors. You determine that.' She also volunteered 'we never truly know the number of contributors in a forensic sample.' The causal limb — 'not independent of the elimination donor's introduction' — is stated by the witness herself: 'I was submitted an elimination sample from Mr. Twiggs… because of that, I determined that there's actually only two individuals, because those small peaks, there was nothing left for a third individual to be compared to.' The ONE genuine counter I found, which the claim forecloses without saying so: the technical reviewer, working the same electropherogram BEFORE the elimination sample arrived, independently notated TWO — 'If I say a number of contributors was three, here she notated that it was two. We had that discussion. She agreed with three.' So a second analyst reached two without Twiggs. That does not falsify the claim (the two-person call that stands in the issued report is the examiner's own, made the next day and attributed by her to the elimination sample), but a reader of the bare claim would not know a second, elimination-independent 'two' exists in the case file. Note also that 'subjective' is the file's characterisation, not the witness's word — her words are 'my determination' and 'best determination'.

session_results.attack: The two quoted times, the wall monitor, the plural "one of the soft interview rooms" and the audio-video recording all verify verbatim, and the P9 correction direction is right (the witness said "one of the soft interview rooms"). What fails is the team label: "an SBI/FBI team" writes a prosecutor out of the flight. Davis names the manifest — two SBI, two FBI, and Ryan McBride of the Utah County Attorney's Office — and McBride is the same prosecutor who examined Faumuina, Bakker and Oliver at this preliminary hearing.
